note_text:
Patient is a 61-year-old with a longstanding history of type 2 diabetes mellitus who presents to the retina clinic for follow-up. Dilated fundus exam of the right eye demonstrates extensive neovascularization of the disc and scattered neovascularization elsewhere, with associated pre-proliferative changes including venous beading and multiple cotton wool spots. There is no evidence of vitreous hemorrhage at this time, but the degree of neovascularization is felt to place the patient at significant imminent risk for vision-threatening complications if left untreated.

Given the severity of the findings and the trajectory of disease progression noted on serial exams over the past several visits, the decision was made to proceed with panretinal photocoagulation of the right eye today rather than continue observation, as the risk of progression to vitreous hemorrhage or tractional retinal detachment now outweighs the risks of laser treatment. The patient was counseled on the procedure, including expected visual side effects such as peripheral field constriction and possible transient decrease in night vision, and provided informed consent.

Procedure: Panretinal (scatter) laser photocoagulation, right eye. Approximately 1400 burns placed in a scatter pattern sparing the macula, using standard settings. Patient tolerated the procedure well without complication. Plan to continue additional sessions as needed and follow up in 4 weeks to assess regression of neovascularization and consider anti-VEGF adjunct therapy if indicated.
